mainTopic: How generously property is transferred: rulings on רבי עקיבא and חכמים, brothers dividing an estate, passage between inner and outer houses, and what comes with a sold house
overview: The משנה just before this argued about a seller who keeps something inside the property he sold. רבי עקיבא holds a seller sells generously, and חכמים hold he sells sparingly. רב rules like חכמים and שמואל rules like רבי עקיבא. רב ירמיה בר אבא's story about רב's silence turns out to fit this, because he had the names in the משנה reversed. רבינא shows that רב and שמואל argue the same way about brothers who divide an estate, and the גמרא explains why both cases had to be stated. רב הונא then admits the הלכה follows שמואל's side, since his students sat near the judges at the ריש גלותא's gate. Next comes a ruling about two houses, one behind the other. The גמרא concludes that when the inner house is given as a gift it comes with a path, because a gift is given generously. Finally a new משנה begins listing what is included when a house is sold: fixed parts yes, movable items no. Its case of a seller who says 'it and everything inside it' continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב rules like the Sages
steps.stepSummary: The ruling reported in the name of רב: the הלכה follows חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is like the words of חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first ruling on the מחלוקת in the משנה. Through רב הונא, רב rules that the הלכה follows חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words that introduce this ruling (רב הונא quoting רב) come just before this text. By siding with חכמים, רב takes the view that a seller does not give away more than he must. He sells sparingly.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical law
Like the words of חכמים (the majority view in the משנה)

phrases.english: The halacha is like the words of the Sages.
phrases.notes: This ruling is רב's, passed on by רב הונא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on the מחלוקת of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, the הלכה follows חכמים.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא reports the opposite ruling in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is like רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, opposite ruling is brought. שמואל says the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two clashing rulings. רב says the הלכה is like חכמים, and שמואל says it is like רבי עקיבא. For רבי עקיבא, a seller sells generously.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who was a student of both רב and שמואל
Like the opinion of רבי עקיבא

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: And Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha is like Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second ruling that opposes the first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רב never objected when I ruled like רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא questions רב הונא's report. He often said in front of רב that the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא, and רב never corrected him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said to רב הונא: But many times I said in front of רב, 'The הלכה is like רבי עקיבא,' and he never said a thing to me!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה בר אבא challenges רב הונא's claim that רב rules like חכמים. רב never objected when he heard a ruling like רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Staying silent when a student states a ruling suggests the teacher agrees. If רב heard 'like רבי עקיבא' many times and stayed quiet, it seems he holds like רבי עקיבא. That would contradict רב הונא's report.

keyTerms.meaning: Many times
In front of רב
And he said nothing at all to me

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said to Rav Huna:
"But many times
I said it in front of Rav:
The halacha is like Rabbi Akiva,
and he did not say anything at all to me!"

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא זִמְנִין סַגִּיאִין אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the report in step 1 of how רב ruled.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's report that רב rules like חכמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב stayed silent when he heard a ruling like רבי עקיבא, so it seems he agreed with רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: How did you recite the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks how רב ירמיה בר אבא recited the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: "How did you learn it?"
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא asks a clarifying question. Which version of the משנה was רב ירמיה בר אבא using?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא suspects the problem is which names were attached to which opinion. If the names were switched, 'like רבי עקיבא' might really mean the view that רב agrees with.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you learn (recite) it?

phrases.english: He said to him: "How did you learn it?"
phrases.notes: רב הונא is asking which name you put on which opinion in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the challenge by asking a clarifying question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which version of the משנה רב ירמיה בר אבא recited in front of רב

steps.title: I learned it reversed
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא admits he recited the משנה with the names switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: "I learned it the other way around."
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה בר אבא answers that in his version, the opinions of רבי עקיבא and חכמים were swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his version, the opinion our משנה gives to חכמים was said in the name of רבי עקיבא. So when he said 'like רבי עקיבא', he actually meant the view our משנה calls חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The opposite, the reverse
I learned / I recited

phrases.english: He said to him: "I learned it the other way around."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He recited the משנה with the names of רבי עקיבא and חכמים switched.

steps.title: That is why רב was silent
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא concludes that רב's silence is no proof. רב agreed with the opinion itself, which really belongs to חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Because of that, he did not say anything to you."
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא resolves the challenge. רב stayed quiet because the ruling he heard was really the view of חכמים, just under a switched name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silence now supports רב הונא's report instead of contradicting it. רב agreed with the opinion itself, whatever name it carried. So the report stands: רב rules like חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of this, for that reason

steps.whatToRemember: רב rules like חכמים and שמואל rules like רבי עקיבא. רב ירמיה בר אבא's story fits this once you know he had the names reversed.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב agreed with רבי עקיבא. He agreed with the opinion he heard, which is the one our משנה calls חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: ״מִשּׁוּם הָכִי לָא אֲמַר לָךְ וְלָא מִידֵּי״.
phrases.english: "Because of that, he did not say anything at all to you."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי לָא אֲמַר לָךְ וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer in step 5 to resolve the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the evidence (the switched names explain the silence)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's silence showed that he holds like רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's silence showed agreement with the opinion of חכמים, which רב ירמיה בר אבא recited under רבי עקיבא's name.

steps.title: Are רב and שמואל following their own reasoning?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי whether this מחלוקת between רב and שמואל matches another מחלוקת of theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Shall we say they each follow their own reasoning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new line of thought. רבינא suggests that רב and שמואל are each consistent with what they say elsewhere. The source for this comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אזדו לטעמייהו' means each אמורא is sticking to a position he holds elsewhere. רבינא is about to show a parallel case about brothers dividing an estate.

keyTerms.meaning: A late אמורא, a colleague of רב אשי
Shall we say? (a suggestion that is being tested)
They follow their own reasoning (from elsewhere)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Shall we say they follow their own reasoning?
phrases.notes: 'They' means רב and שמואל from the steps above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about how consistent the two rulings above are.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב and שמואל's positions here match their positions in another מחלוקת

steps.title: שמואל: brothers who divide keep no rights in each other's share
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes שמואל. Brothers who divide an estate have no rights of passage, ladders, windows or water channels in each other's portions, and he stresses that these are fixed laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: Brothers who divided have no path against each other, no ladders against each other, no windows against each other, and no water channel against each other. And be careful with these, for they are fixed halachos.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the source behind רבינא's suggestion. שמואל rules that when brothers split their father's property, neither one keeps any rights in the other's part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Brothers who divide are treated like sellers to each other. Saying they keep no rights means each gives his share fully and generously. That fits שמואל's ruling like רבי עקיבא that a seller sells generously.

keyTerms.meaning: Brothers who divided (their father's estate)
A right of way through the other's land
Ladders, the right to set them up on the other's land
Windows, the right to keep light coming in
A water channel
Fixed, firmly established laws

phrases.english: As Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel:
Brothers who divided
phrases.notes: They split up the property they inherited from their father.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהֶן לֹא דֶּרֶךְ זֶה עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: have no path against each other,
phrases.notes: Neither may walk through his brother's part to reach his own, even if they did so in their father's lifetime.

phrases.english: nor ladders against each other,
nor windows against each other,
phrases.notes: Neither can stop his brother from building a wall that blocks his windows.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אַמַּת הַמַּיִם זֶה עַל זֶה.
phrases.english: nor a water channel against each other.
And be careful with these,
for they are fixed halachos.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that supports רבינא's suggestion in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל holds a seller (or a dividing brother) gives generously
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן quoting שמואל on brothers who divide an estate

steps.title: רב: brothers do keep these rights
steps.stepSummary: רב disagrees with שמואל and says the brothers do keep these rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב said: They do have them.
steps.whatsHappening: The other side of the parallel מחלוקת. רב holds that brothers who divide keep their rights of passage, ladders, windows and water channels in each other's portions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of שמואל. For רב, each brother gives only what he must and keeps his rights, just as חכמים hold that a seller sells sparingly. Now both sides of the parallel are in place, and רבינא's suggestion seems to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: They have them (they keep these rights)

steps.whyThisMatters: With both opinions laid out, the pattern is clear: שמואל says generous transfer, and רב says sparing transfer. This is the parallel רבינא's question is testing.

phrases.english: And Rav said: They do have them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means all four rights just listed: path, ladders, windows and water channel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the parallel source by giving רב's opposing view.
steps.raayaObject: That רב holds a seller (or a dividing brother) gives sparingly and keeps his rights
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that brothers who divide keep these rights

steps.title: Why רב's view also had to be stated in the house-sale case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says both cases were needed. If we only had the brothers case, we might think רב holds his view only there, because a brother can say he wants to live as his fathers did. In a regular sale רב might agree with שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to teach both. If we had only been taught the brothers case, I would say that רב rules this way only there, because the brother can say: 'I want to live in it the way my fathers lived in it.' You can see this idea in the פסוק: 'Instead of your fathers shall be your sons.' But in the house-sale case, I would say רב agrees with שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: Steps 8-9 showed that רב and שמואל argue in two different cases. Now the גמרא explains why we need to hear the argument in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers case has a special reason for keeping the old rights: a son wants to keep the house the way his father had it. That reason does not apply when a stranger buys a house. So the brothers case alone would not tell us that רב also disagrees in the sale case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (both statements are needed)
It taught us
To live (in a place)
My fathers, my ancestors
Know that it is so (introduces support)
Agrees, concedes

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. The גמרא is only explaining why the same מחלוקת had to be stated twice.

phrases.english: It is necessary (to state both);
for if it had taught us only in that case,
phrases.notes: 'That case' means the brothers who divided their father's estate.

phrases.english: I would say that only in that case does רב say so,
because he can say to him:
I want to live in it
just as my fathers lived in it;
know that this is so, for it is written:
'Instead of your fathers shall be your sons';
but in this case,
phrases.notes: 'This case' means an ordinary sale of a house.

phrases.english: I would say he agrees with שמואל;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the brothers-case מחלוקת quoted in steps 8-9 does not make the house-sale מחלוקת unnecessary.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case teaches something the other cannot
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the brothers case alone, רב might agree with שמואל in an ordinary sale.
steps.terutzMaskana: The brothers case has its own reason (living as one's fathers did), so the sale case must be stated separately.

steps.title: Why שמואל's view also had to be stated in the brothers case
steps.stepSummary: The reverse also holds. If we had only the sale case, שמואל might rule only there and agree with רב about brothers. So both cases are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had been stated only in the sale case, I would say that only in that case does שמואל say so. But in the brothers case, I would say he agrees with רב. Therefore both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכותא by showing the other direction. The sale case alone would not tell us שמואל's view about brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a sale, שמואל holds the seller gives up the rights, and he does not keep a path for himself. But brothers have the special wish to live as their fathers did, so שמואל might give in there. Since each case could change the other side's view, the גמרא needs both.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it had been stated: a 'what if', not a real new teaching
In that one

steps.whatToRemember: Each case adds something: brothers have a family reason to keep the old rights, and a sale has its own logic. So רב and שמואל had to argue in both.

phrases.english: And if it had been stated only in this case,
phrases.notes: Here 'this case' means the house sale. The last 'this case' in the line switches to the brothers.

phrases.english: I would say that only in that case does שמואל say so,
but in this case (of the brothers),
I would say he agrees with רב;
therefore it is necessary (to state both).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא from step 10 in the opposite direction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the sale case alone, שמואל might agree with רב about brothers.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases are needed, so the double מחלוקת is justified.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks whose view is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רב הונא whether the הלכה follows his side or רב הונא's side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רב הונא: Is the הלכה like us, or is the הלכה like you?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the מחלוקת is clear, רב נחמן asks how we actually rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question moves from understanding the argument to deciding it in practice. 'Us' and 'you' refer to the two sides, שמואל's and רב's.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical law
Like us, according to our view
Like you (plural), according to your view

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: רב נחמן said to רב הונא:
Is the הלכה like us,
or is the הלכה like you?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא: הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתִין, אוֹ הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתַיְיכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the מחלוקת is explained, this step asks for the practical ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה follows שמואל's view or רב's view in these property cases.

steps.title: רב הונא rules like רב נחמן's side
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the הלכה follows רב נחמן's side, because they are close to the ריש גלותא's court, where judges are often found.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The הלכה is like you, because you are close to the gate of the ריש גלותא, where judges are found.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the ruling, even though it goes against his own side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is experience. People who are around working judges know money law better, so their view is followed here. This means the הלכה follows שמואל: brothers who divide an estate keep no rights in each other's portions.

keyTerms.meaning: Gate
The Exilarch, leader of the Jews in בבל
Judges
Are commonly found

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows שמואל's side in these cases, because his students were close to the judges and knew money law well.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical ruling for brothers who divide an estate and for house sales.

phrases.english: He said to him: The הלכה is like you,
for you are close to the gate of the ריש גלותא,
where judges are found.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה follows רב נחמן's side (שמואל), because they are experienced in money law through their closeness to the judges.

steps.title: Two houses one behind the other
steps.stepSummary: A new teaching: if two houses, one behind the other, are both sold or both given as gifts, neither owner has a right of way through the other. This is even more true if the outer one was a gift and the inner one was sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: Two houses, one behind the other. If both were sold, or both were given as gifts, they have no right of way through each other. All the more so when the outer one was given as a gift and the inner one was sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about passage rights between an inner house and an outer house that came from the same owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When both houses go out the same way, both owners got the same strength of rights, so the inner owner cannot claim a path through the outer house. If the outer house was a gift, it is even clearer, because a gift is given more generously than a sale. So the outer owner surely got the house free of any path.

keyTerms.meaning: Further in than this one, behind it
Sale
Gift
Right of way, path
All the more so
Outer / inner

steps.confusionAlert: The 'all the more so' case is outer house as a gift and inner house as a sale. Don't flip them. The generous gift goes to the outer house, which makes a path for the inner owner even less likely.

phrases.english: It was stated: Two houses
one behind the other;
phrases.notes: The only way out of the inner house is through the outer one.

phrases.english: if both were sold, or both were given as gifts,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהֶן דֶּרֶךְ זֶה עַל זֶה.
phrases.english: they have no right of way through each other.
All the more so if the outer one was a gift
and the inner one was sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: שְׁנֵי בָתִּים זֶה לְפָנִים מִזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related topic about passage rights between houses transferred from one owner.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two houses, one behind the other, transferred both by sale or both by gift: neither has a right of way through the other. All the more so if the outer was a gift and the inner a sale.

steps.title: First assumption: outer house sold, inner house given, no right of way
steps.stepSummary: Some חכמים first understood that if the outer house was sold and the inner house was given as a gift, neither owner has a right of way through the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the outer house was sold and the inner house was given as a gift, some understood from this that they have no right of way through each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the one case not yet covered: outer house sold, inner house given as a gift. It reports what some people first thought, which sets up the next step where the גמרא will reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 covered both houses sold, both given, and outer given with inner sold. In all of those there is no right of way. Here some assumed the last mix, outer sold and inner given, works the same way, so the inner owner may not walk through the outer house.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer house, the one closer to the street
The inner house, which can only reach the street through the outer one
They understood from this, a first assumption that is often rejected
A right of way, a path to walk through

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a first assumption. The very next words, וְלָא הִיא, reject it. The final ruling is that the inner owner does have a path.

phrases.english: The outer one by sale and the inner one by gift
they understood from this:
phrases.notes: This is what some חכמים thought at first. The גמרא is about to disagree.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהֶן דֶּרֶךְ זֶה עַל זֶה;
phrases.english: they have no right of way through each other;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 14 to the remaining mixed case and states a first assumption about it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First assumption: when the outer house is sold and the inner is given, the inner owner has no path through the outer house.

steps.title: Rejected: a gift is given generously, so the inner owner gets a path
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the assumption. A משנה teaches that a giver includes everything because a gift is given generously, so the person who gets the inner house as a gift also gets a path.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is not so. Didn't we learn in a משנה: When is this said? With a seller. But one who gives a gift gives all of them. This shows that one who gives a gift gives generously. Here too, one who gives a gift gives generously.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the first assumption is wrong and proves it from a משנה that shows gifts are given generously.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that a seller of a field does not automatically include certain extras, but a giver includes everything. The reason is that a giver gives with a generous eye. So the owner who gave away the inner house surely meant to include a path to it through the outer house.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so, a rejection of what was just said
Didn't we learn in a משנה? Introduces a proof
In what case are these words said? Limits an earlier rule
Apparently, so we see
With a generous eye, giving freely and fully

steps.whatToRemember: A seller gives only what is clearly included, but a giver gives generously. So in the case of outer house sold and inner house given, the inner owner does have a right of way.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a gift is given בְּעַיִן יָפָה is a general rule. It helps decide what is included whenever property is given away instead of sold.

phrases.english: But it is not so
didn't we learn in a משנה:
In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: This משנה, found later in the מסכתא, is about extras that a person selling a field does not automatically include.

phrases.english: With one who sells,
but with one who gives a gift
he gives all of them?
Apparently, one who gives a gift
gives with a generous eye;
here too, one who gives a gift
gives with a generous eye.
phrases.notes: So the giver meant for the inner house to come with a path through the outer house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first assumption of step 15 using a proof from a משנה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the assumption that there is no right of way when the outer house is sold and the inner is given
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The assumption treated a gift like a sale. A gift is given generously and includes the path.

steps.title: משנה: what is included when selling a house
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that selling a house includes the parts fixed to it, like the door, a fixed mortar and the lower millstone. It does not include movable items like the key, a movable mortar, the upper stone, the oven or the stove.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who sells a house has sold the door but not the key. He has sold the fixed mortar but not the movable one. He has sold the lower millstone but not the upper stone. He has not sold the oven or the stove.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists which things come with a house when it is sold and which do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is that items attached to the house are part of the house, and items that can be moved are not. The key goes with the door but is still movable, so it is not included. The oven and stove count as movable, so they are not sold with the house.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, our משנה
A mortar fixed into the ground
Movable, something that can be carried away
The fixed lower base of a mill
The movable upper part of the mill, where grain is poured in
A double stove with two openings for pots

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the key comes with the house just because the door does. The door is attached, but the key is movable, so it stays with the seller.

phrases.english: משנה
One who sells the house
has sold the door,
but not the key;
he has sold the fixed mortar,
but not the movable one;
he has sold the lower millstone,
but not the upper stone;

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַתַּנּוּר וְלֹא אֶת הַכִּירַיִם.
phrases.english: and not the oven and not the double stove.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, what is included in the sale of a house
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling a house includes the parts fixed to it but not the movable items in it.

steps.title: משנה: when the seller says 'it and everything inside it'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins a new clause about a seller who says he is selling the house and everything inside it. The ruling comes in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he said to him: 'It and everything inside it'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up a new case: the seller says he is selling the house together with everything in it. The ruling for this case continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the משנה described a plain sale of a house. This clause changes the case: the seller openly includes everything inside, which may change what the buyer gets.

keyTerms.meaning: When he said to him, introduces a different case
It and everything inside it, wording that includes more in the sale

phrases.english: When he said to him:
"It and everything that is inside it"

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: הוּא וְכׇל מַה שֶׁבְּתוֹכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a second clause of the same משנה, a sale that openly includes the contents
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the case of a sale of a house 'with everything inside it'. The ruling follows in the continuing text.
